related_questions.question: What is required to enter the United States?

text_blocks.snippet: To enter the United States, foreign nationals generally need a valid passport and a U.S. visa, unless they are from a visa-exempt country and qualify for the Visa Waiver Program. Additionally, they may need to demonstrate they meet specific requirements for their purpose of travel, such as tourism, work, or study.
snippet_highlighted_words: a valid passport and a U.S. visa

list.snippet: A passport is a mandatory document for international travelers to the USA, regardless of the purpose of travel.
It must be valid for at least six months beyond your intended stay in the U.S., unless you are from a country with a specific agreement waiving this requirement.
Ensure your passport has at least two blank pages for entry and exit stamps.
Most foreign nationals need a visa to enter the U.S.
Visas are categorized based on the purpose of travel, such as tourist visas (B-2 or B1/B2), student visas (F1), work visas, etc.
You'll need to apply for the appropriate visa based on your travel purpose.
The U.S. Department of State's website provides comprehensive information on visa types and application procedures.
Citizens of certain countries may be eligible to enter the U.S. without a visa under the Visa Waiver Program.
This program allows eligible travelers to enter the U.S. for tourism or business for a limited time (usually 90 days).
To participate in the Visa Waiver Program, you'll need to meet specific requirements, including holding a passport from a participating country and completing an ESTA application.

list.title: Proof of sufficient funds:
list.snippet: You may need to demonstrate you have enough money to support yourself during your stay in the U.S.

list.title: Proof of ties to your home country:
list.snippet: This could include documents like employment verification, property ownership, or school enrollment to show you have a reason to return home.

list.title: Specific requirements for certain types of travel:
list.snippet: For example, students or exchange visitors will need to provide additional documentation related to their program.

list.title: Compliance with U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) regulations:
list.snippet: Be prepared to answer questions from CBP officers about your trip and provide any necessary documentation.
